Blood Sugar Field Notes

A deterministic fixture page for tiling experiments: hero, prose, cards, a long table, a tall chart, an image grid, and a footer, in one tall document.

1. Why banding cuts matter

This section is ordinary prose. A band boundary landing in the middle of a paragraph forces the vision model to judge a half-sentence, and a boundary landing mid-heading is worse: the model must decide whether a decapitated heading is a defect or an artifact of the crop itself.

Every element on this page has a stable position once rendered, no animation runs, and all assets are inline, so two renders of this file should be near-identical. That property is what the digest-stability half of the experiment measures.

The prose block continues for a few paragraphs so that at least one fixed 1400-pixel cut lands inside it. Padding paragraphs follow: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog, again and again, each line adding vertical extent to the section so the geometry is realistic rather than toy-sized.

Cinnamon, chromium, and berberine walk into a systematic review. The punchline depends on the confidence interval. Readers aged seventy-six prefer the punchline in eighteen-point type with generous line height, which is why this fixture uses larger body text than a typical engineering blog.

2. Card grid

Fasting glucose

Baseline 141 mg/dL, week eight 118 mg/dL. The delta is the number the reader remembers.

A1C

Baseline 7.9%, week twelve 7.1%. Hero metric of the page, and of most testimonials.

Post-meal spike

Peak excursion narrowed from 210 to 164 mg/dL after the protocol change.

Morning routine

Two capsules before breakfast, water first, walk after. Compliance beats optimization.

Sleep

Seven hours median. The overnight dawn-effect rise shrank once dinner moved earlier.

Support tickets

Most common question: can it be taken with metformin. The answer requires the doctor.

4. Tall chart (taller than one band)

5. Callouts and short prose

Compliance note. Statements on this fixture are synthetic test data, not health claims. The layout mimics the real thing; the numbers are invented.

Short section, deliberately: it creates several natural gaps in a row, giving the snapping algorithm easy targets right after the hardest region on the page.

Design note. Two callouts separated by one paragraph produce three clean gaps within roughly four hundred vertical pixels.
